The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Fix the oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and an inertial
chart of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use signature
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, length coordinates
$x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres, and coordinate time $t$ in seconds as in
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Greek spacetime indices run
from $0$ to $3$; spatial indices run from $1$ to $3$ and are contracted with
the Euclidean spatial metric. The coordinates $x^a$ have unit metre and
$\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

The positive constants $c$, $h$ and $e_{\rm SI}$ have the exact SI defining
values; write $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has SI unit
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined under the current SI;
no exact numerical value or current estimate for it is adopted. Put
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ when that symbol is used. These are SI
normalization inputs, not empirical claims about a selected QFT model.

For a species with rest mass $m_{\rm rest,SI}>0$ in kilograms define its
inverse-length mass parameter

$$\mu:=\frac{m_{\rm rest,SI}c}{\hbar}\quad[\mathrm m^{-1}].$$

For a spatial wave vector $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, with each component in
$\mathrm m^{-1}$ and the Euclidean norm, define
$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k):=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}\in\mathbb R_{>0}$, with
unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Here $\omega_\mu$ is the temporal wave number, not the
SI angular frequency; the corresponding SI angular frequency is
$c\omega_\mu$. Energy and momentum are $E=\hbar c\omega_\mu$ in joules and
$\mathbf p=\hbar\mathbf k$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. With
$p=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k)\in\mathbb R^4$ and
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$, the phase convention is

$$p\mathbin{\circ}x:=\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$

For a selected local action represented on a chart region
$\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ by
$$\frac{S}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathcal U}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\,d^4x,\quad d^4x:=dx^0dx^1dx^2dx^3,$$
the natural Lagrangian density $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-4}$. Since $x^0=ct$, the corresponding SI Lagrangian density is
$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{SI}}:=\hbar c\,\mathcal L_{\mathrm{nat}}$ and has unit
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. This unit conversion alone does not identify a
Lagrangian density with the model's Hamiltonian energy density.

For canonical engineering dimensions in this four-dimensional normalization,
use the formal field symbols $\phi_{\rm n}$ and $\psi_{\rm n}$ in the selected
scalar and Dirac kinetic terms, assigning them length degrees $-1$ and
$-3/2$, respectively. These are the dimensions fixed by those free kinetic
terms, not exact scaling dimensions of interacting fields: anomalous
dimensions, when present, are separate quantities. These symbols do not
assert pointwise field maps or operator fields; a model supplies its field
space and regularity. Let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ and
$F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}$ use the component convention of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], namely
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, with
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$ only when a potential is
supplied. Define the normalized photon potential and field strength by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have length degrees $-1$ and $-2$, respectively. The EM supplier is used
only for SI units and tensor components: no classical Maxwell equation,
Lorentz-force law, or classical-to-quantum identification is adopted here.

For any separately declared SI charge parameter $q_{\rm SI}$ in coulombs put

$$q_{\rm n}:=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}.$$

It is dimensionless. For the positive exact SI elementary charge use
$e_{\rm n}:=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$ and define the rationalized
dimensionless coupling $\alpha:=e_{\rm n}^2/(4\pi)$. Since $\mu_0$ is
measured, these formulas do not assign an exact numerical value to
$e_{\rm n}$ or $\alpha$. If the model uses minimal coupling, its convention is
$D_\mu=\partial_\mu-iq_{\rm n}a_\mu$; for an electron with
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ this reads $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+ie_{\rm n}a_\mu$.
Bare, renormalized-at-scale, and measured effective charges are separately
labelled model parameters; applying the conversion to one label does not
identify it with either of the others or specify a running law.

In a supplied four-component spinor representation, let
$\gamma^a\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb C^4)$, $a=0,1,2,3$, be
dimensionless linear maps satisfying
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}:=\gamma^a\gamma^b+\gamma^b\gamma^a
=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$, where $I_4$ is the identity map. Set $\beta:=\gamma^0$
and $\alpha^i:=\beta\gamma^i$; then $\beta^2=I_4$ and
$\gamma^i=\beta\alpha^i$. For a supplied four-component spinor $\psi$ write
$\bar\psi:=\psi^\dagger\beta$. The effective Clifford metric is $-\eta$.
A supplied free Dirac model may use
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi=0$ for its model-supplied spinor field
$\psi$; that model supplies its field domain and regularity. The phase and
Clifford choices are conventions; this item proves no representation or field
equation.

For the autonomous evolution convention, assume Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice
function. Let a selected model supply a complex Hilbert space $\mathscr H$
as in [[def-hilbert-space]] and a time-independent complex-linear Hamiltonian
$H:D(H)\to\mathscr H$ with a specified dense linear domain
$D(H)\subseteq\mathscr H$ and SI energy
unit joules. Require self-adjointness as in
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]: $H=H^*$,
including equality of domains and values. Here $y\in D(H^*)$ precisely when
there is a $z\in\mathscr H$ such that
$\langle Hx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle$ for every $x\in D(H)$, and
$H^*y=z$; density makes $z$ unique.

The published mathematical supplier
[[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]]
then supplies the spectral measure $E_H$ on the Borel subsets of
$\mathbb R$. This is a normalized projection-valued measure as in
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]: its values are bounded orthogonal
projections, $E_H(\mathbb R)=I$, $E_H(B\cap C)=E_H(B)E_H(C)$, and it is
countably additive in norm on every vector. For $\xi\in\mathscr H$ put
$\nu_\xi(B):=\langle E_H(B)\xi,\xi\rangle$, a finite positive measure.
The spectral integral of $\lambda$ represents $H$, on exactly the domain
$D(H)=\{\xi\in\mathscr H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,d\nu_\xi(\lambda)<\infty\}$.
For real $t$ in seconds define the autonomous evolution by bounded Borel
functional calculus,
$$U(t):=\exp(-itH/\hbar):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda).$$
The spectral variable $\lambda$ carries unit joule. This exponential is a
bounded operator on all of $\mathscr H$, even when $H$ is unbounded; it
does not mean an operator power series on arbitrary vectors. The supplier
gives a strongly continuous unitary group: $U(0)=I$,
$U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $\|U(t)\xi-U(t_0)\xi\|\to0$ as $t\to t_0$ for
each $\xi\in\mathscr H$. A model may restrict it to a declared
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Each $U(t)$ is a surjective complex-linear map
satisfying $\langle U(t)\xi,U(t)\zeta\rangle=\langle\xi,\zeta\rangle$
for all $\xi,\zeta\in\mathscr H$; write $U(t)^*:=U(t)^{-1}$. The exponent
is dimensionless because $\hbar$ has unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. For any
model-supplied complex-linear operator $O:D(O)\to\mathscr H$, with specified
linear domain $D(O)\subseteq\mathscr H$, define its Heisenberg conjugate by
$$O_H(t):=U(t)^*O\,U(t),\quad D(O_H(t)):=\{\xi\in\mathscr H:U(t)\xi\in D(O)\}.$$
The model supplies the Hamiltonian and operator domains; the spectral supplier
justifies this evolution only for those data and hypotheses. This dictionary
constructs no model-specific Hamiltonian or field representation and does not
adopt a physical dynamics law. Where a free-field
module uses an inner product linear in its second variable, convert to the
repository's first-variable-linear pairing by
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\rm FF}=(v,u)_{\rm root}$.

For precision about domains, let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space with
inner product linear in its first variable and let
$\mathscr D\subseteq\mathcal H$ be a dense complex linear subspace. A **weak operator-valued distribution
on the common domain $\mathscr D$** means a complex-linear assignment
$g\mapsto\Phi(g)$ for $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$, where each
$\Phi(g):\mathscr D\to\mathcal H$ is linear and, for every
$u,v\in\mathscr D$, the scalar map
$g\mapsto\langle\Phi(g)u,v\rangle$ is a continuous complex-linear functional
on the test-function space with the topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]], hence a distribution as in [[def-distribution]].
This definition gives no pointwise field $\Phi(x)$ and no product
$\Phi(x)\Phi(x)$; a product or extension needs a separate construction. It
asserts only matrix-element continuity and the stated linear maps; all further
operator properties, locality, local observable algebras, graded locality,
and gauge-specific potential behavior must be supplied by a constructed
model. Test-function units can be chosen so a specified smeared observable is
dimensionless; there is no universal test-function unit asserted here.

Primitive data for a selected model include its species and rest masses,
declared charge parameters, regulator geometry, couplings, state and any
constructed measurement data. Vacuum-subtracted Hamiltonians, regulator
eigenvalues, distributions, correlations and outcome probabilities are
derived only when their constructions supply the required domains and
well-definedness. This dictionary neither constructs an interacting
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space nor asserts pointwise field products,
scattering, an LSZ limit, asymptotic completeness, or removal of a regulator.

Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. A **non-Abelian gauge datum on $M$** consists of the following specified objects.

First choose a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$ that is compact in its manifold topology (every open cover has a finite subcover) and noncommutative (there are $g,h\in G$ with $gh\ne hg$). The actual group $G$, including its global form, is part of the datum. Its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$ with the bracket transported from left-invariant smooth vector fields.

Choose a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$: the projection and right action are smooth, the action is free and transitive on each fibre, and there are local trivializations $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times G$ that are equivariant diffeomorphisms over each open $U\subseteq M$.

Choose a specified set $I$ of representation labels and, for each $a\in I$, a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V_a$, a positive-definite Hermitian form $h_a$, and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho_a:G\to U(V_a,h_a)$. Here $U(V_a,h_a)$ is the group of complex-linear isometries of $h_a$, and a representation is the corresponding finite-dimensional group action. Its associated vector bundle is the quotient $E_a=P\times_{\rho_a}V_a$ with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho_a(g)v]$.

Two smooth right principal $G$-bundles over $M$ are isomorphic over $M$ when a smooth diffeomorphism between their total spaces covers $\operatorname{id}_M$ and commutes with the right $G$-actions. A **bundle sector** is one equivalence class under this relation. The datum specifies a set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors and requires $[P]\in\Sigma$; a model may take $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The Lie algebra alone does not replace the chosen group or sector. This definition does not choose a connection, an action functional, or a quantum theory.

A finite-regulator effective-field-theory model-data record consists of a finite undirected graph Γ=(X,EΓ) with nonempty vertex set X, the graph distance dΓ, retained real coordinates ℓ∈ℝ^X, integrated real coordinates χ∈ℝ^X, a Borel ultraviolet action SUV(ℓ,χ)∈ℝ, and a specified Borel probability measure νH on ℝ^X for the integrated coordinates. The full ultraviolet data are these objects before any integration. This definition does not assert that the integral of exp(−SUV) exists; finiteness and positivity are checked when the Wilsonian action is defined.

For the positive heavy-scalar Gaussian submodel, include a real symmetric matrix A on ℝ^X satisfying uᵀAu≥0 for every u and Axy=0 when dΓ(x,y)>1. Its entries have mass-squared units and its operator norm satisfies √‖A‖≤Λ. Choose M>0 and put K=M²I+A. The heavy coordinate χ has mass-inverse units, so χᵀKχ is dimensionless. A source J(ℓ)∈ℝ^X has mass units, so J(ℓ)ᵀχ is dimensionless. When the source is restricted to external energy E, require J(ℓ)=PEJ(ℓ), where PE is the orthogonal spectral projection of A onto eigenvalues in [0,E²].

The scale data are a positive Wilsonian matching scale $\mu_W$, a heavy mass $M>0$, an external energy bound $E\ge0$, and a regulator cutoff $\Lambda>0$, with $\sqrt{\|A\|}\le\Lambda$ in the Gaussian submodel. The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$ records where the retained low-coordinate action is specified; $M$ is the heavy quadratic mass; $E$ bounds the admitted source spectrum; and $\Lambda$ bounds the finite regulator. These are separately named parameters, and this definition imposes no relation among their numerical values. A small-remainder theorem may require an additional hierarchy such as $E<M$.

Light and heavy name the roles in the declared split: ℓ is retained at μW and χ is integrated in the finite measure νH. They do not assert that every retained field is massless or that every integrated field is heavy in an unrestricted continuum theory. If the model includes non-Abelian gauge data, record the actual global group, Lie algebra, principal bundle, representations, and admitted bundle sectors as one supplied gauge-data object. That object selects no connection, action, or quantum measure by itself. The Gaussian submodel below keeps any such gauge data as fixed context and makes no gauge-field integration claim.

This is a finite-dimensional regulator description. It makes no assertion that a general interacting functional measure exists, that a cutoff can be removed, or that any selected model describes nature.

Take a finite-regulator model datum with retained coordinates $\ell$, integrated coordinates $h$, a normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_H$ on the finite-dimensional $h$-space, and a real Borel ultraviolet action $S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)$. For each retained configuration $\ell$ define

$$
Z_H(\ell):=\int e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)}\,d\nu_H(h).
$$

On the domain of $\ell$ for which $0<Z_H(\ell)<\infty$, the finite-regulator Wilsonian action at scale $\mu_W$ is

$$
S_W(\ell;\mu_W):=-\log Z_H(\ell).
$$

Thus “integrating out” the high sector means this specified finite integral over $h$ while $\ell$ is held fixed. The measure, action, regulator, and low/high split are inputs; the definition does not assert that every interacting model has a finite or well-defined integral. Replacing $\nu_H$ by a positive constant multiple changes $S_W$ only by an additive constant independent of $\ell$, which is fixed by the chosen normalization convention.

A one-particle-irreducible effective action, when it exists, is the Legendre transform of a connected source-generating functional for the retained fields. It is a different construction from the high-coordinate integral above. No 1PI functional is needed or asserted here.

derivations.claim: The identity $A^0=I$ has range zero. If $A^r$ has range at most $r$, then $(A^{r+1})_{xy}=\sum_{z\in X}(A^r)_{xz}A_{zy}$. A nonzero summand requires $d_\Gamma(x,z)\le r$ and $d_\Gamma(z,y)\le1$, so the triangle inequality gives $d_\Gamma(x,y)\le r+1$. Induction yields range at most $r$ for every $A^r$.

Each term of $S_N$ is a scalar multiple of $A^r$ with $r\le N$. Therefore every matrix entry of $S_N$ vanishes when $d_\Gamma(x,y)>N$. It is a finite-range approximation to the finite-regulator Wilsonian kernel; no convergence or generic remainder follows from this range calculation.

finite_checks: For N=0, S0=M^-2 I has range zero; step 1.1 proves range at most r for each finite power A^r.
The range assertion is proved exactly in steps 1.1–2.1; no convergence test is used.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC and let $d\ge1$. For a real symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, write $\gamma_C=N_d(0,C)$, allowing singular $C$. For a nonnegative Borel function $f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty]$, define the normalized shell transform
$$T_Cf(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x+z)\,d\gamma_C(z)\in[0,\infty].$$

all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Then countable choice holds. Moreover, if $R\subseteq X\times X$ is serial on a nonempty set X and $a\in X$, there is a sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $x_0=a$ and $x_n R x_{n+1}$ for every n. Thus the countable and dependent choices required by the probability-product suppliers are available under AC.

Use natural units c=ℏ=1, with physical dimensions assigned using the QFT unit convention of the selected model. A finite-regulator effective-field-theory model-data record consists of a finite undirected graph Γ=(X,EΓ) with nonempty vertex set X, the graph distance dΓ, retained real coordinates ℓ∈ℝ^X, integrated real coordinates χ∈ℝ^X, a Borel ultraviolet action SUV(ℓ,χ)∈ℝ, and a specified Borel probability measure νH on ℝ^X for the integrated coordinates. The full ultraviolet data are these objects before any integration. This definition does not assert that the integral of exp(−SUV) exists; finiteness and positivity are checked when the Wilsonian action is defined.

For the positive heavy-scalar Gaussian submodel, include a real symmetric matrix A on ℝ^X satisfying uᵀAu≥0 for every u and Axy=0 when dΓ(x,y)>1. Its entries have mass-squared units and its operator norm satisfies √‖A‖≤Λ. Choose M>0 and put K=M²I+A. The heavy coordinate χ has mass-inverse units, so χᵀKχ is dimensionless. A source J(ℓ)∈ℝ^X has mass units, so J(ℓ)ᵀχ is dimensionless. When the source is restricted to external energy E, require J(ℓ)=PEJ(ℓ), where PE is the orthogonal spectral projection of A onto eigenvalues in [0,E²].

The scale data are a positive Wilsonian matching scale $\mu_W$, a heavy mass $M>0$, an external energy bound $E\ge0$, and a regulator cutoff $\Lambda>0$, with $\sqrt{\|A\|}\le\Lambda$ in the Gaussian submodel. The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$ records where the retained low-coordinate action is specified; $M$ is the heavy quadratic mass; $E$ bounds the admitted source spectrum; and $\Lambda$ bounds the finite regulator. These are separately named parameters, and this definition imposes no relation among their numerical values. A small-remainder theorem may require an additional hierarchy such as $E<M$.

Light and heavy name the roles in the declared split: ℓ is retained at μW and χ is integrated in the finite measure νH. They do not assert that every retained field is massless or that every integrated field is heavy in an unrestricted continuum theory. If the model includes non-Abelian gauge data, record the actual global group, Lie algebra, principal bundle, representations, and admitted bundle sectors as one supplied gauge-data object. That object selects no connection, action, or quantum measure by itself. The Gaussian submodel below keeps any such gauge data as fixed context and makes no gauge-field integration claim.

This is a finite-dimensional regulator description. It makes no assertion that a general interacting functional measure exists, that a cutoff can be removed, or that any selected model describes nature.

Take a finite-regulator model datum with retained coordinates $\ell$, integrated coordinates $h$, a normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_H$ on the finite-dimensional $h$-space, and a real Borel ultraviolet action $S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)$. For each retained configuration $\ell$ define

$$
Z_H(\ell):=\int e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)}\,d\nu_H(h).
$$

On the domain of $\ell$ for which $0<Z_H(\ell)<\infty$, the finite-regulator Wilsonian action at scale $\mu_W$ is

$$
S_W(\ell;\mu_W):=-\log Z_H(\ell).
$$

Thus “integrating out” the high sector means this specified finite integral over $h$ while $\ell$ is held fixed. The measure, action, regulator, and low/high split are inputs; the definition does not assert that every interacting model has a finite or well-defined integral. Replacing $\nu_H$ by a positive constant multiple changes $S_W$ only by an additive constant independent of $\ell$, which is fixed by the chosen normalization convention.

A one-particle-irreducible effective action, when it exists, is the Legendre transform of a connected source-generating functional for the retained fields. It is a different construction from the high-coordinate integral above. No 1PI functional is needed or asserted here.

In the finite graph model, a matrix $B$ on $\mathbb R^X$ has range at most $r$ when $B_{xy}=0$ whenever $d_\Gamma(x,y)>r$. The positive heavy-sector matrix $A$ from the model data has range at most one. A derivative expansion of its inverse kernel is the formal operator series

$$
(M^2I+A)^{-1}\sim M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(-A/M^2)^r.
$$

Its order-$N$ truncation, for an integer $N\ge0$, is the finite operator

$$
S_N:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^r.
$$

It has range at most $N$ in this regulator. For a source $J$ supported in the spectral interval $[0,E^2]$ of $A$, the dimensionless power-counting parameter is $E/M$. This definition is an organized finite-order approximation; it does not assert convergence for unrestricted sources, a generic error bound, or a continuum local-operator expansion. The positive Gaussian theorem supplies a remainder bound only under its exact hypotheses.

Assume AC. Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $A:D(A)\subseteq H\to H$ be densely defined, self-adjoint and nonnegative, and let $M>0$. Set $K=M^2I+A$ on $D(A)$ and let $E_A$ be the spectral measure of $A$. Define $f_M(a)=(M^2+a)^{-1}$ for $a\ge0$. The bounded spectral operator $f_M(A)$ is the inverse $K^{-1}$ and satisfies $\|K^{-1}\|\le M^{-2}$. For $J\in H$ define the matched quadratic effective-action contribution
$$\Delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}(J):=-\tfrac12\langle J,K^{-1}J\rangle.$$
The inner product is the complex Hilbert pairing, linear in its first variable; the displayed quadratic form is real and nonpositive. In natural units $\hbar=c=1$, $A$ and $K$ have mass-squared units; normalize the source/pairing so $\langle J,K^{-1}J\rangle$ is dimensionless, hence $\|J\|^2$ has mass-squared units. In a finite real regulator, integration of $\exp[-\tfrac12\chi^TK\chi+j^T\chi]$ divided by the zero-source Gaussian integral yields $\exp[\tfrac12j^TK^{-1}j]$, so the corresponding effective action changes by $-\tfrac12j^TK^{-1}j$. Since $\log$ is the inverse of $\exp$ on positive reals, taking $-\log$ of that normalized integral gives this effective-action contribution. Determinants and Lebesgue integration are finite-regulator quantities only; this definition supplies no infinite-dimensional Gaussian measure or determinant.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $j\in\mathbb R^d$. Let $\gamma_{K^{-1}}=N_d(0,K^{-1})$, where covariance is the matrix $\mathbb E[XX^T]$. Then
$$\frac{\int_{\mathbb R^d}\exp(-\tfrac12x^TKx+j^Tx)\,dx} {\int_{\mathbb R^d}\exp(-\tfrac12x^TKx)\,dx} =\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{j^Tx}\,d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(x) =\exp\!\left(\tfrac12j^TK^{-1}j\right).$$
Equivalently, in the finite real Gaussian regulator with normalized weight $e^{-S}$ and $\hbar=1$, completing the source shift $\chi=K^{-1}j+\eta$ gives
$$\tfrac12\chi^TK\chi-j^T\chi=\tfrac12\eta^TK\eta-\tfrac12j^TK^{-1}j.$$
Use $\hbar=1$ and coordinate/source units for which $x^TKx$ and $j^Tx$ are dimensionless. Both integrals are finite; their common Gaussian normalization cancels in the ratio. No infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure or determinant is asserted.

Assume the hypotheses and notation of the positive heavy-mode Gaussian matching data. Let $E\ge0$ be an energy and let $P_E:=E_A([0,E^2])$ be the spectral projection of $A$. For $J=P_EJ\in H$ and an integer $N\ge0$, define
$$S_NJ:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^rJ,$$
which is well-defined since $J$ has bounded spectral support. Put $R_NJ:=K^{-1}J-S_NJ$. Then
$$\|R_NJ\|\le M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}\|J\|,$$
and
$$\left|\Delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}(J)+\tfrac12\langle J,S_NJ\rangle\right| =\tfrac12|\langle J,R_NJ\rangle| \le \frac{\|J\|^2}{2M^2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}.$$
Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$: $A$ has units of mass squared, $E,M$ have mass units, and $E^2/M^2$ is dimensionless. Under the source normalization of the positive heavy-mode Gaussian matching data, $\|J\|^2/M^2$ and the action remainder are dimensionless. These are exact conditional bounds for every $E\ge0$; the truncation is small/useful when $E<M$. No claim is made for unrestricted sources or arbitrary interacting matching.

derivations.claim: For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $x^TKx=M^2\|x\|^2+x^TAx>0$, so $K$ is symmetric positive definite and the finite Gaussian supplier applies. On the complexification, real symmetry makes $A$ self-adjoint; for $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$, the cross terms in $\langle x+iy,A(x+iy)\rangle$ cancel because $x^TAy=y^TAx$, leaving $x^TAx+y^TAy\ge0$. Thus the positive-operator hypotheses of [F4] also hold.

In the model specialization [A3], $e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell_*,\chi)}=e^{J(\ell_*)^T\chi}=e^{J^T\chi}$ and $d\nu_H(\chi)=d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(\chi)$. Therefore the Wilsonian integral in [F2] is exactly
$$
Z_H(\ell_*)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell_*,\chi)}\,d\nu_H(\chi)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{J^T\chi}\,d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(\chi)=Z_H(J).
$$
By [F5] and step 1.1 this value is finite and strictly positive, so $\ell_*$ lies in the domain of the Wilsonian-action definition. Hence $S_W(\ell_*;\mu_W)=-\log Z_H(\ell_*)=-\log Z_H(J)=\Delta S_W(J)$. At zero source the normalized Gaussian integral is $1$, so this is also the source-induced action increment with zero baseline; no determinant factor remains.

By [F4] and step 2.1, the heavy Gaussian effective-action contribution equals $\Delta S_W(J)$. Apply [F6] to the band-limited source $J=P_EJ$ and the positive operator verified in step 1.1; its vector and action inequalities are the two displayed remainder bounds. When the additional condition $E<M$ holds, the factor $E^2/M^2$ is less than one and the bound decreases geometrically with $N$. This conclusion is conditional and remains within the finite Gaussian sector.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the finite-regulator model data in the definitions below. Let $d\ge1$, let $A$ be a real symmetric positive-semidefinite $d\times d$ matrix, let $M>0$, and put $K=M^2I+A$. Use natural units with $\chi$ in mass-inverse units, $A$ and $K$ in mass-squared units, and a source $J\in\mathbb R^d$ in mass units. Let $E\ge0$, let $P_E$ be the spectral projection of the complexification of $A$ onto $[0,E^2]$, and assume $J=P_EJ$. In the finite Gaussian sector, let $\gamma_{K^{-1}}=N_d(0,K^{-1})$ and define

$$ Z_H(J):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{J^T\chi}\,d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(\chi) $$

$$ \Delta S_W(J):=-\log Z_H(J) $$

For each integer $N\ge0$, put

$$
S_NJ:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^rJ.
$$

Then both finite Gaussian integrals are finite and

$$ Z_H(J)=\exp\!\left(\tfrac12J^TK^{-1}J\right) $$

$$ \Delta S_W(J)=-\tfrac12J^TK^{-1}J $$

The inverse-kernel and action remainders satisfy

$$
\|K^{-1}J-S_NJ\|\le M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}\|J\|,
$$

$$ \left|\Delta S_W(J)+\tfrac12J^TS_NJ\right| \le \frac{\|J\|^2}{2M^2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1} $$

These are exact conditional statements for a finite positive quadratic heavy sector. The remainder is small in the stated band when $E<M$; no claim is made for unrestricted sources, arbitrary interactions, a continuum measure, or a differentiated Wilsonian flow.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $C_1,C_2$ be real symmetric positive-semidefinite $d\times d$ covariance matrices, and let $f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty]$ be Borel. For a covariance matrix $C$, let $\gamma_C$ denote the centered Gaussian probability with covariance $C$, including when $C$ is singular, and define

$$
T_Cf(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x+z)\,d\gamma_C(z).
$$

For a finite nonnegative Borel potential $V$, $0<T_C(e^{-V})(x)\le1$; define the finite nonnegative potential $V_C(x):=-\log T_C(e^{-V})(x)$. Then

$$
T_{C_2}(T_{C_1}f)(x)=T_{C_1+C_2}f(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d)
$$

as an equality in $[0,\infty]$, and

$$
e^{-(V_{C_1})_{C_2}(x)}=e^{-V_{C_1+C_2}(x)}.
$$

The Gaussian measures are normalized probabilities, so no determinant or vacuum constant appears. This is a finite-regulator composition identity; it asserts no derivative equation along a covariance path and no continuum limit.

Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

Assume AC and let $d\ge1$. For a real symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, write $\gamma_C=N_d(0,C)$, allowing singular $C$. For a nonnegative Borel function $f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty]$, define the normalized shell transform
$$T_Cf(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x+z)\,d\gamma_C(z)\in[0,\infty].$$
This is a Borel function of $x$. If $V:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ is finite-valued and Borel, define
$$V_C(x):=-\log\bigl(T_C(e^{-V})(x)\bigr).$$
Then $V_C$ is a finite nonnegative Borel function, and $0<T_C(e^{-V})(x)\le1$ for every $x$. The covariance convention is $\mathbb E[ZZ^T]=C$. derivations.claim: Here $K=5m_0^2$ is positive, $J$ is an eigenvector of $A$ with eigenvalue $E^2=m_0^2$, and $E<M$. Thus $K^{-1}J=1/(5m_0)$ and $S_0J=M^{-2}J=1/(4m_0)$. By [F1], $Z_H(J)=e^{1/10}$ and $\Delta S_W=-1/10$, while the order-zero action is $-\tfrac12J^TS_0J=-1/8$.

Take a finite-regulator model datum with retained coordinates $\ell$, integrated coordinates $h$, a normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_H$ on the finite-dimensional $h$-space, and a real Borel ultraviolet action $S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)$. For each retained configuration $\ell$ define

$$
Z_H(\ell):=\int e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)}\,d\nu_H(h).
$$

On the domain of $\ell$ for which $0<Z_H(\ell)<\infty$, the finite-regulator Wilsonian action at scale $\mu_W$ is

$$
S_W(\ell;\mu_W):=-\log Z_H(\ell).
$$

Thus “integrating out” the high sector means this specified finite integral over $h$ while $\ell$ is held fixed. The measure, action, regulator, and low/high split are inputs; the definition does not assert that every interacting model has a finite or well-defined integral. Replacing $\nu_H$ by a positive constant multiple changes $S_W$ only by an additive constant independent of $\ell$, which is fixed by the chosen normalization convention.

A one-particle-irreducible effective action, when it exists, is the Legendre transform of a connected source-generating functional for the retained fields. It is a different construction from the high-coordinate integral above. No 1PI functional is needed or asserted here.
